overlays.notes: Measured 2026-07-13 from the protocol's own stats API: total collateral value $71,324,392 against total BOLD supply 29,047,740 gives a system collateralization ratio of 2.455; Stability Pool deposits of 19,111,283 BOLD against the same supply give a liquidation capacity ratio of 0.658. The dedicated qualitative review on 2026-07-15 used Liquity's current documentation and implementation pinned at commit c8a5a4ee2e9dc024905856b6698a77d849c68c7e. Each branch has its own Stability Pool; liquidation burns deposited BOLD against debt and redistributes any remainder only among active Troves in that branch. That establishes an adequate two-stage backstop and adequate operational branch isolation, while the shared BOLD claim still exposes holders to unrecovered debt from any branch and prevents a strong rating. A branch can permanently shut down below its SCR or on oracle failure, stop interest and new borrower operations, and enable urgent branch redemptions. Liquity's own risk disclosure nevertheless states that collapsed collateral can leave unbacked BOLD with no unconditional recapitalization facility, so shutdown and bad-debt handling is limited. Any BOLD holder can permissionlessly redeem through the CollateralRegistry for a routed mix of collateral at protocol value, with urgent redemption available after branch shutdown, supporting adequate structural redemption.

overlays.notes: Measured on-chain 2026-07-14 at finalized Ethereum block 25533257 via journaled eth_call (evidence: shared/data/safety-score-v9/mechanism-measurements/lusd-liquity/2026-07-14-block-25533257.json; producer scripts/maintenance/measure-cdp-mechanism-metrics.ts, byte-replay verified). The contract graph was derived on-chain from the LUSD token (troveManagerAddress(), stabilityPoolAddress(), then TroveManager.priceFeed()) rather than from a published address list. TroveManager.getTCR at the canonical protocol price - an eth_call simulation of PriceFeed.fetchPrice() = 1875.88242714 USD/ETH, agreeing 0.0000% with the Chainlink ETH/USD feed - returned 5.033 (derivation check: getTCR == floor(coll x price / debt), exact). An earlier same-day read at block 25530791 used the frozen lastGoodPrice (1780.21673094, about 5.1% stale in the quiet system) and gave 4.776; superseded by owner decision D2 on 2026-07-14. StabilityPool.getTotalLUSDDeposits() over getEntireSystemDebt() gives a liquidation capacity ratio of 0.278; LUSD totalSupply() equals getEntireSystemDebt() exactly at the pinned block, so the ratio is identical against supply. checkRecoveryMode() was false, MCR 110%, CCR 150%. The pinned implementation and official documentation establish that Stability Pool deposits burn liquidated debt and that any residual debt and collateral are redistributed across active Troves, supporting an adequate backstop design while the measured 27.8% committed-capital ratio remains visible. Liquity V1 is one immutable ETH-only Trove system, so cross-branch isolation is structurally not applicable. Recovery Mode changes liquidation rules but the protocol has no shutdown or unconditional recapitalization facility, supporting limited shutdownAndBadDebt quality. Any holder can permissionlessly redeem LUSD for protocol-priced ETH from the lowest-collateralized Troves, supporting adequate structural redemption.

overlays.notes: Measured on-chain 2026-07-14 at HyperEVM block 40440545 via eth_call. The contract graph was derived on-chain: the feUSD token exposes no Liquity getters (it is a role-gated upgradeable ERC20, not Liquity's BoldToken), so the graph was taken from the CollateralRegistry proxy 0x9de1e57 (impl 0xD06DfC33), whose totalCollaterals() = 4 and getTroveManager(i)/getToken(i) enumerate exactly four branches: WHYPE (TM 0x3100F4e7), UBTC (TM 0xbbe5f227), kHYPE (TM 0x7c07bB77), wstHYPE (TM 0x58446C58). The registry address is corroborated by Felix's own docs, and each TroveManager's activePool() matches the four holders already in the coin file's liveReservesConfig. Per branch, getEntireBranchColl() x PriceFeed.lastGoodPrice() over getEntireBranchDebt(): WHYPE 430,173.636 WHYPE @ $65.20795344 = $28,050,742 vs debt 9,522,352.500 (CR 2.946); UBTC 28.055 @ $62,449.56855 = $1,752,006 vs debt 569,059.981 (CR 3.079); kHYPE 75,231.740 @ $64.98626 = $4,889,029 vs debt 1,123,782.912 (CR 4.351); wstHYPE 10,395.891 @ $65.41448 = $680,042 vs debt 348,425.553 (CR 1.952). System totals: collateral $35,371,819 over total branch debt 11,563,620.946 feUSD = collateralizationRatio 3.059. Cross-checks: (1) Felix's TroveManager has no getTCR(uint256), so collateral was verified three ways — TroveManager.getEntireBranchColl() equals ActivePool.getCollBalance() equals the collateral ERC20's balanceOf(ActivePool) for all four branches (exact, to within 1 wei on WHYPE); (2) re-valuing the same collateral at the live PriceFeed.fetchPrice() instead of lastGoodPrice() gives CR 3.070, agreeing to within 0.4%; (3) total branch debt 11,563,620.946 versus feUSD totalSupply() 11,563,588.435 agree to 0.0003% — supply is 32.51 feUSD BELOW debt, which is the expected direction for Liquity V2 (branch debt includes interest accrued but not yet minted), not a discrepancy. DefiLlama independently reports 11,563,600.69 circulating. liquidationCapacityRatio = sum of StabilityPool.getTotalfeUSDDeposits() (the fork's rename of getTotalBoldDeposits) 9,915,239.353 over total debt = 0.857; each pool's deposits plus getYieldGainsOwed() reconcile exactly against feUSD.balanceOf(StabilityPool), confirming the deposit figure is committed capital actually held, not an accounting claim. IMPORTANT QUALIFIER: Stability Pools are branch-local and cannot cross-subsidize, and coverage is very uneven — UBTC's pool holds 3.572x its own branch debt while wstHYPE holds only 0.238x and WHYPE 0.703x. Capping each branch's usable pool at its own debt gives a branch-isolation-adjusted ratio of 0.731; the reported 0.857 is the brief's uncapped sum-over-total definition and is the optimistic bound. Parameters read on-chain from each BorrowerOperations: MCR 135% / CCR 170% / SCR 120% for WHYPE, kHYPE and wstHYPE, and MCR 125% / CCR 150% / SCR 120% for UBTC. All four branches are live (shutdownTime() = 0) and on their primary oracle (PriceFeed priceSource = 0, i.e. not fallen back to lastGoodPrice). Liquidation penalties are not exposed by any public getter. Felix's docs and pinned implementation establish an independent state contract per branch, a branch-local Stability Pool with residual debt and collateral redistributed only to that branch's active troves, system redemption through the CollateralRegistry, and SCR-triggered branch shutdown with urgent redemption. Backstop and branch isolation are adequate; structural redemption is adequate. Shutdown and bad-debt handling are limited because shutdown, urgent redemption, and redistribution are implemented, but no separate recapitalization facility covers a branch-wide collateral deficit and the documented external control is Anthias monitoring.

Component evidence: collateralizationParameters (limited) — Per-pair CDP accounting is on-chain (getPairAccounting borrow + collateral shares; convertToAssets for vault claim). System CR only ~1.076 at pin — thin buffer versus conventional overcollateralized CDPs. Collateral is layered ERC-4626 claims on crvUSD/frxUSD lending markets at accounting par, not direct blue-chip collateral.; liquidationMechanics (adequate) — Insurance Pool documentation: on liquidation the pool buys collateral with reUSD (burned), liquidated collateral routes through LiquidationHandler which withdraws underlying from the lending pool when liquidity allows (can retry). Dual-source: Insurance Pool CDP Liquidations section + on-chain InsurancePool capital committed at pin (7.91% of debt).; backstop (limited) — Insurance Pool is the explicit bad-debt and liquidation backstop (docs + 2.546M reUSD on-chain). If bad debt exceeds the pool, docs state the protocol assumes residual bad debt and leftover collateral is held by the protocol — no unconditional external recapitalization. Limited depth at 7.91% of debt.; branchIsolation (limited) — Pairs are separate contracts with distinct collateral vaults (19 registry addresses observed). Redeemer may choose which pools to redeem against (Stability Mechanics). Cross-pair transmission exists via shared Insurance Pool and communal redemption. Limited isolation: pair-level accounting exists but insurance and redemptions are system-shared.; shutdownAndBadDebt (limited) — Defined bad-debt path: Insurance Pool purchases impaired collateral and burns reUSD; residual beyond the pool is assumed by the protocol with collateral held for pool holders to withdraw (Insurance Pool Bad Debt section). No dual-sourced global settlement/emergency shutdown. Limited, not adequate.; structuralRedemption (limited) — Communal redemption model with ~1% fee establishing a price floor (Stability Mechanics docs): redeemer burns reUSD against borrower collateral across chosen pairs with weighted discounts. Access is conditional (operator/oracle-price guard on RedemptionHandler per prior pinned implementation family). Limited structural redemption rather than unconditional 1:1 cash redeem..

overlays.notes: Pinned Celo block 72202914; journaled evidence: shared/data/safety-score-v9/mechanism-measurements/audm-mento/2026-07-15-block-72202914.json. The producer enumerated all 16 live exchange IDs, found the configured token/USDm pair exactly once, and measured 10000000 USDm of counter-bucket capacity at a 15 bps spread. Conversion capacity is an analogous exit metric only and is not relabeled as collateralization or liquidation capital. Completion pass 2026-07-20 (backstop, branchIsolation, shutdownAndBadDebt added; all prior components, metrics, and sources preserved and both source URLs re-fetched and re-read this session): the Celoscan page confirms the pinned contract is the verified Mento BiPoolManagerProxy, and the Mento V3 documentation establishes that Mento conversion pools quote an oracle rate through a Chainlink-only oracle path, that trading limits cap flow per token over time, and that circuit breakers trip and halt trading when stablecoins move too far off peg or other safety thresholds are breached, with USDm/EURm backed by the shared Mento Reserve. Backstop is limited: the measured 10000000 USDm virtual counter-bucket is bounded conversion inventory, and the shared reserve backing USDm is not an AUDm-dedicated committed backstop. Branch isolation is limited: per-pair buckets bound AUDm/USDm flow, but the Broker, USDm counter-asset, shared reserve, and oracle paths are failure domains shared with other Mento stables. Shutdown and bad-debt handling is limited: BreakerBox circuit breakers and trading limits can halt unsafe conversion, but no unconditional residual-deficit recapitalization or holder settlement path is documented for AUDm. No prior quality tier was changed; the added components follow the same limited pattern as sibling Mento conversion-token overlays. NOT established: any AUDm-dedicated insurance fund or stability pool, any documented reserve commitment earmarked for AUDm residual deficits, and any formal shutdown or wind-down settlement procedure for AUDm holders.

overlays.notes: 2026-07-20 review. Zephyr Protocol is a Monero-fork chain running a Minimal-Djed reserve design: ZSD is minted and redeemed directly against the ZEPH base coin held in the on-chain protocol reserve, and ZRS reserve shares form the equity/first-loss tranche. There are no borrowing positions and no liquidations in the design — peg defense is mint gating plus an always-permitted redemption path — so the liquidationMechanics component and the liquidationCapacityRatio metric are structurally not-applicable. Whitepaper rules: new ZSD cannot be minted when the reserve ratio is below 400% (dual spot and moving-average ratios must both pass, an anti-manipulation variation on stock Djed); ZRS minting halts above 800% to prevent dilution; the ZRS price falls toward PminRC below 400% to incentivize recapitalization; redeem_stable is always permitted, paying oracle value while the reserve ratio is >= 1 and a pro-rata share of the reserve if it ever falls below 1 (stable-holder haircut as the terminal bad-debt rule). Post-audit hardfork v11 renamed asset types to ZPH/ZSD/ZRS/ZYS per the protocol documentation. MEASUREMENT from the protocol's own reserve snapshot API (captured 2026-07-19T23:46:28Z at reserve_height 822991): ZEPH reserve 4,450,016.09, ZSD circulation 422,029.10, ZRS circulation 2,632,087.36, spot price $0.46573515 per ZEPH; reserve assets = 4,450,016.09 x 0.46573515 = $2,072,528.91 against $422,029.10 ZSD liabilities (equity $1,650,499.79) giving the protocol-reported reserve_ratio of 4.910867 on spot and 4.537806 on the moving average. collateralizationRatio is reported as the spot reserve ratio 4.910867; the moving-average figure 4.537806 is the binding mint-gate value. NOT ESTABLISHED: the snapshot API is the protocol's own self-reported scanner and no independent third-party attestation of the reserve was found; the oracle operator set and its decentralization were not established; ZRS secondary-market depth (real recapitalization capacity) was not established; no shutdown or wind-down mechanism exists in the design.

liquidationCapacityRatio.rationale: Djed-style reserve design with no borrowing positions and no liquidation engine: ZSD is minted and redeemed directly against the protocol reserve under reserve-ratio gates (400% min mint, 800% max), so there is no liquidation pool whose capacity could be measured.

liquidationMechanics.rationale: No liquidation mechanism exists in the Djed-style design: there are no loans or margin positions; stability is enforced by reserve-ratio mint gates and always-permitted redemption against the protocol reserve.

branchIsolation.rationale: Single-collateral (ZEPH-only), single-reserve Djed design: there are no branches or isolated markets to segregate.

overlays.notes: CLAIM AND SEGREGATION (limited). Polymarket's documentation states that pUSD is a standard ERC-20 wrapper that 'represents a USDC claim', that wrapping and unwrapping are enforced onchain by the CollateralOnramp and CollateralOfframp contracts, and that there is no algorithmic peg and no fractional reserve; the documented unwrap path is a permissionless external call releasing USDC.e to any holder. The claim is therefore code-enforced and documented in official protocol documentation. It is limited rather than adequate because no binding legal document establishes a holder claim on segregated reserve assets: the Terms of Use page is JavaScript-rendered and only its footer legal disclosure was retrievable (identifying the operating entities — Adventure One QSS Inc. internationally, and QCX LLC d/b/a Polymarket US as a CFTC-regulated Designated Contract Market for the US platform), with no trust, segregation, or bankruptcy-remoteness language for pUSD reserves located in any retrieved source. CUSTODY CONTINUITY (limited). The reserves are not held at any custodian: backing USDC/USDC.e sits in the on-chain backing vault contract 0xc417fd8e9661c0d2120b64a04bb3278c17e99db1 on Polygon, verified by eth_call at block 90551185 (2026-07-20T07:16 UTC) to hold 630,114,454.459495 USDC.e plus 313.420408 native USDC. There is no rehypothecation path in the documented current design (wrap-only mint against deposited collateral), and administrative change is gated: at block 90551639, pUSD owner() returned Timelock 0x47ebfac3353314c788b96cdcbf41daadfe03629c whose minDelay() returned 43200 seconds (12 hours). Continuity therefore rests on immutable contract custody plus a timelocked admin — documented and on-chain verified, but with no custodian diversification and with upgrade-key risk, hence limited. ASSURANCE AND RECONCILIATION (adequate). A complete direct on-chain assets-and-liabilities reconciliation was performed at Polygon block 90551185: pUSD totalSupply 629,375,893.36934 against vault-held 630,114,767.879903 USDC-equivalent, a coverage ratio of approximately 1.00117 — every outstanding pUSD is matched by verifiable on-chain collateral with a small surplus, and this reconciliation is continuously reproducible by any party against public RPC data. In addition, the official contracts registry links two independent third-party audits of the CTF Exchange V2 system (Quantstamp and Cantina, both March 2026) and a live Cantina bug bounty. Per the on-chain reconciliation precedent this supports adequate; it is not strong because no independent financial-statement examination or attestation exists and the reconciliation here is self-performed. NOT ESTABLISHED: any legal segregation, trust, or bankruptcy-remoteness for pUSD reserves; the full Terms of Use text bearing on pUSD (page shell only was retrievable); whether the Quantstamp/Cantina reports cover the CollateralToken contract specifically (reports linked from the official docs but their per-contract scope was not re-verified); the identity/signers of the governance Safe behind the 12-hour Timelock.

On-chain reads via eth_call at each chain's latest block ~2026-07-20T06:25-06:45Z (Ethereum finalized block 25572002 via https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com; BSC via https://bsc-dataseed.binance.org; Kaia via https://public-en.node.kaia.io; Berachain via https://rpc.berachain.com; Mantle via https://rpc.mantle.xyz; Sonic via https://rpc.soniclabs.com). The BSC PoolManager (0xC757E47d6bC20FEab54e16F2939F51Aa4826deF7) configures LTV 6000 but threshold 7500 (75%, diverging from the documented 90%) and its debt-token slot is BSC USDa 0x9356086146be5158E98aD827E21b5cF944699894 (18 dec). MEASUREMENT: summed getPoolManagerReserveInformation() across the six deployed pool managers - collateral (BTC, 8 dec): Ethereum 1,364.01; BSC 2,416.59896725; Kaia 30.0; Mantle 0.00003296; Sonic 0.00055677; Berachain 0 => 3,810.60955698 BTC, valued at the protocol's own oracle = 244,095,793.75 USD; debt (in each pool's debt-token units, USD-denominated): Ethereum 46,970,257.61 USDT (6 dec); BSC 85,195,290.23 USDa (18 dec); Sonic 11.25 USDa; Berachain 42,579 raw treated as <=42,579 USD dust; Kaia and Mantle zero => 132,165,559.13 USD total. collateralizationRatio = 244,095,793.75 / 132,165,559.13 = 1.846894 (Ethereum-only 1.860203; BSC-only 1.817038). QUALITY RATIONALE: collateralizationParameters adequate (documented LTV/thresholds verified against deployed configs on two chains and a live oracle within 0.11% of Chainlink; the BSC 75% threshold diverges from the 90% docs and liquidation amounts are operator-discretionary rather than contract-enforced, keeping this below strong). liquidationMechanics limited (the HFT-on-centralized-exchanges process is documented and matches the verified onlyOwner liquidate(), but execution is fully operator-discretionary with no permissionless or on-chain-auction path and no independent verification of execution quality). backstop limited (no contractual reserve or insurance fund is documented anywhere; docs reference CeFi liquidity providers and institutional support, which are non-binding self-reported claims; the interface ToS further disclaims custody and loss responsibility at the interface level; onlyOwner liquidate in the verified source), so no on-chain pool or permissionless bidder set is contractually committed to absorb liquidations; the ratio is structurally undefined for this design. NOT ESTABLISHED: independent verification of the custodied BTC (no published custody addresses were found, and the pools' collateral fields are protocol bookkeeping rather than token balances); any reserve/insurance fund with binding terms; conversion-vault funding and throughput; coverage of the non-EVM Movement deployment and any pools beyond the six measured; reconciliation of pool-reported debt (132.2M USD) to total USDa supply (~148M USD per project tracking) - the gap is consistent with USDT 1:1-minted USDa and unmeasured deployments but is unproven; why BSC's liquidation threshold (75%) diverges from the documented 90%.

overlays.notes: Measured 2026-07-20 at Ethereum block 25572058 via eth_call over https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com, cross-checked against Inverse's own stats APIs fetched the same hour (fixed-markets at 06:04:58Z, FiRM TVL at 06:11:17Z). SCOPE: DOLA issuance is FiRM-Fed dominated — the on-chain FiRM Fed (0x2b34548b865ad66a2b046cb82e59ee43f75b90fd) globalSupply() read 97,584,203.48 DOLA = 96.73% of the 100,888,118.24 DOLA totalSupply() at the same block, and the markets API reconciles exactly: sum(totalDebt) 42,982,751.71 + sum(idle market dolaLiquidity) 54,602,362.64 = 97,585,114.36, within 0.001% of globalSupply (unaccrued drip timing). The PSM Fed currently issues nothing (PSM supply() = 0). collateralizationRatio = 1.305242 = FiRM total collateral TVL $56,102,913.11 (Inverse f2/tvl API) over FiRM DOLA debt $42,982,751.71 (Inverse fixed-markets API); this is a FiRM-branch measurement — DOLA minted but sitting idle inside market contracts (54.6M) is protocol inventory, not outstanding debt, and the residual ~3.3M of legacy-Fed supply (incl. unresolved 2022 Frontier bad debt whose current amount was NOT established) carries no dedicated collateral. Analogous supply-wide ratio 0.55609 (= TVL / total DOLA supply) is reported for transparency, not used as the metric. COLLATERALIZATION PARAMETERS (adequate): every FiRM market has governance-set collateral factor, liquidation factor, liquidation incentive, minDebt, ceiling, and rolling 24h borrow limits — observed live in the API across 45 markets (collateralFactor 0.30-0.92, liquidationFactor 0.326-1.0, liquidationIncentive 0.04-0.12) and documented as market parameters in the liquidations documentation; pricing runs through the documented Pessimistic Price Oracle (lower of current Chainlink price vs 48h low), with staleness thresholds halting new borrows and an EOA/whitelist borrow gate. Parameters are governance-mutable with no third-party attestation of their adequacy, so adequate rather than strong. LIQUIDATION MECHANICS (adequate): documented permissionless third-party liquidators repay DOLA debt (up to the market liquidation factor) and seize collateral plus the market liquidation incentive; depleted-DBR positions first accrue debt via forced replenishment at a documented 54.75% APR (10% of the replenishment cost to the caller) until liquidation eligibility. Incentive parameters verified in the API; no liquidation was stress-tested this session. liquidationCapacityRatio is structurally not-applicable: FiRM liquidations are funded by external liquidators, and no DOLA-dedicated pool is contractually committed to fund liquidation repayments (the jrDOLA vault absorbs post-liquidation bad-debt shortfalls — evidenced under backstop — it does not fund liquidations). BACKSTOP (limited): jrDOLA (0x633821b8e003344e5223509277f2084ea809a452, on-chain name 'Junior Dola', asset() = sDOLA) is a documented ERC-4626 first-loss vault whose sDOLA assets the FiRMSlashingModule (0x3b1E443aB423c9A7B1B2EA7b3cB7c0be012a4FbF) can slash to repay FiRM bad debt before protocol reserves; but at block 25572058 the vault held only 438.754496 sDOLA (totalAssets) = ~614.99 DOLA, i.e. 0.00001431 of FiRM debt — the committed buffer is currently negligible. Slashing also requires a governance-or-guardian trigger, covers only governance-approved FiRM markets, and explicitly excludes the PSM; residual losses beyond the vault fall on unquantified protocol reserves. Limited for the material size/coverage gaps despite a well-documented, audited (dual Sherlock, per docs) design. BRANCH ISOLATION (adequate): documented Personal Collateral Escrows give each user a dedicated escrow per collateral market, so a compromised market cannot touch collateral in other markets; the API confirms a per-market escrowImplementation and isolated market contracts. Bad debt is still mutualized to the whole system via jrDOLA/reserves, so adequate rather than strong. SHUTDOWN AND BAD DEBT (limited): the documented path is liquidation shortfall -> jrDOLA slash -> protocol reserves, and the DBR documentation states DBR xy=k auction proceeds currently repay outstanding bad debt from the 2022 Frontier exploit (a real, documented recapitalization route, but slow and revenue-dependent); no global DOLA shutdown or holder settlement path is documented, and the current outstanding bad-debt amount was not established this session. STRUCTURAL REDEMPTION (limited): the PSM (0x4dfd662622d766304cb539e66f893c4defa19398; verified source read via Routescan) offers permissionless DOLA->USDS swaps at 1:0.998 (on-chain sellFeeBps = 20, buyFeeBps = 0, vault() = sUSDS 0xa3931d71877C0E7a3148CB7Eb4463524FEc27fbD) — but supply() read 0 at block 25572058, so current redemption capacity is zero, and USDS is external Sky collateral, not protocol collateral. No redemption of DOLA for FiRM collateral exists. NOT ESTABLISHED this session: any committed liquidation-funding pool; the size/composition of protocol reserves beyond jrDOLA; the outstanding legacy Frontier bad-debt figure; independent verification of the Inverse stats APIs' TVL/debt figures (issuer-published numbers cross-checked against on-chain Fed supply only); liquidation behavior under stress (no live or historical liquidation replay). REASSESSMENT 2026-07-22 (Pharos honesty-downgrade ruling, owner-accepted): the 2026-07-22 FiRM fixed-markets API pull pinned at Ethereum block 25584925 (see dola-inverse-finance.json reserveReview) shows FiRM's non-Frontier DOLA debt is now dominated by DOLA-paired Curve LP collateral markets (sUSDe-DOLA, yv-sUSDe-DOLA, sUSDS-DOLA, yv-sUSDS-DOLA, yv-USR-DOLA, and scrvUSD-sDOLA), which together sum to 41,158,275.29 of the 42,981,164.82-DOLA non-Frontier debt denominator (95.8%). Each of these markets pairs its named stablecoin with DOLA itself inside a Curve pool, so roughly half of the posted collateral value is endogenous DOLA rather than an independent external asset, and liquidation proceeds from these markets are reflexively priced off DOLA's own peg rather than an outside reference; this downgrades both COLLATERALIZATION PARAMETERS and LIQUIDATION MECHANICS from adequate to limited. Separately, the Frontier Fed's 2,749,310.09 DOLA of outstanding legacy debt (ctoken totalBorrows, ~2.75M DOLA, unchanged from the 2022 exploit) remains unresolved with no established repayment path beyond the slow, revenue-dependent DBR-auction route, while the jrDOLA first-loss vault backstop remains negligible (~615 DOLA against the debt base per the 2026-07-20 on-chain read, i.e. essentially zero coverage). An unresolved ~2.75M-DOLA bad-debt overhang against a first-loss buffer that rounds to zero downgrades SHUTDOWN AND BAD DEBT from limited to weak.

liquidationCapacityRatio.rationale: FiRM liquidations are funded by permissionless external liquidators who repay DOLA debt in exchange for collateral plus the market liquidation incentive; there is no DOLA-dedicated pool contractually committed to fund liquidation repayments. The jrDOLA first-loss vault absorbs post-liquidation bad-debt shortfalls (evidenced under the backstop component; ~615 DOLA at block 25572058) rather than funding liquidations, so no committed liquidation-capacity ratio exists.

overlays.notes: CLAIM AND SEGREGATION (limited). overlays.notes: Evidence base (all pages fetched and read 2026-07-20; existingOverlay was null, so this is a fresh entry). AZND overview establishes AZND is the senior tranche of a GHAM-managed Asia credit Asset Pool, 'protected from losses by first-loss credit tranche'. The yield-mechanics page establishes the documented mandate: Asia-Pacific government bonds (min BBB), corporate IG (min BBB-), bank senior and subordinated debt (average min issuer rating BBB), high yield (min BB), and private credit co-lent with other large financial institutions, managed by Golden Hill Asset Management, described as a Singapore regulated fund manager; GHAM's own published commentary corroborates that GHAM holds MAS Capital Markets Services Licence CMS101035 as a Licensed Fund Management Company (manager self-publication; the MAS FID page itself was not scrapeable in this session, so regulator-direct confirmation was not obtained). The risk-management-framework page establishes: illiquid private credit capped at 20% (minimum 80% liquid freely tradable bonds), blended portfolio rating target of BBB or higher, duration managed to an average of 5, maturity ladders and staggered durations, and prime-broker credit lines for fast liquidity. The mint/redeem page establishes KYC-gated 1:1 minting in USDC/USDT/AUSD and a weekly Singapore fund redemption calendar (~7 calendar days; processed by Tuesday for settlement the following week), with sub-threshold instant redemptions from an onchain liquidity buffer. The muBOND page establishes muBOND as the first-loss credit tranche over the same portfolio and documents that muBOND NAV price updates are 'expected to be published weekly at inception with the frequency intended to increase over time'. The price-stability-mechanism page establishes the tranching design (muBOND documented as ~15% of total protocol TVL absorbing portfolio losses before AZND) and an Insurance Fund that is only 'intended' to be funded from protocol fees over time. The transparency page establishes Pennyworks as the independent NAV accounting partner for the Asset Pool and that onchain Treasury Wallets are segregated from the company's operational funds. The Terms of Use (Oct 2025 PDF) establish a contractual redemption right ('These Digital Tokens can be subsequently redeemed for stablecoins'), that AZND/muBOND can only be minted and redeemed through the Platform, and a processing period of up to ten (10) business days, while disclaiming that Mu Digital is a financial institution/fund management platform and disclaiming fiduciary duties. On-chain reads via the Monad public RPC at block 88947418 measured AZND totalSupply 16,326,375.99 (matching the canonical supply figure) and muBOND totalSupply 927,145.60, i.e. the junior first-loss token equals only ~5.7% of senior AZND supply in token-unit terms (analogousMetrics.muBondJuniorTrancheShareOfSeniorSupply), materially below the documented ~15%-of-TVL design target; muBOND reprices with accrued yield so its USD share may be somewhat higher than the token-unit ratio, but no published NAV conversion was found. Metrics: weightedAverageMaturityDays = 1825 uses the risk framework's documented 'average duration of 5' (years) portfolio target - this is the only portfolio time-horizon figure Mu Digital publishes; it is average duration, NOT a disclosed weighted-average maturity (no WAM or weighted-average-life figure exists in the reviewed disclosures), and for non-amortizing bonds duration understates contractual maturity, so 1825 should be read as a lower bound on the true maturity horizon. valuationCadenceDays = 7 uses the documented weekly muBOND NAV repricing plus the documented weekly fund redemption calendar; an explicit standalone NAV-strike frequency for the fund itself is not separately published, and the weekly figure is stated with 'expected/intended' language at inception. Quality rationale: every component is rated limited because all structural evidence is issuer self-disclosure (litepaper + ToS) with no published fund-administrator reports, no named custodian, no holdings-level or ratings-mix disclosure, and no prospectus/SPV documentation of a holder claim on the fund assets; where the documented first-loss size (~15% of TVL) contradicts the on-chain measured junior share (~5.7%), the lower tier was kept per the when-in-doubt rule. NOT established (left out of claims): custodian bank/prime broker identity and segregation terms of the fund vehicle; any SPV, trust, or bankruptcy-remoteness documentation giving AZND holders a direct claim on Asset Pool assets; existence and size of the Insurance Fund (only an intention is documented); published Pennyworks NAV reports; current portfolio holdings, ratings mix, and actual maturity profile; rehypothecation terms.

Terms of Use establish the protocol is unregulated, disclaims custody of user funds, and lists oracle/smart-contract risk. overlays.notes: Measured at finalized Ethereum block 25571938 via public RPC https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com (eth_call). The Aave Umbrella documentation establishes that Umbrella is Aave's automated safety module: staked assets are burned/slashed to cover protocol deficits in the same asset-network pair without governance intervention, GHO staking is supported on Ethereum, a governance-configured per-asset deficit offset lets the DAO absorb a first tranche before stakers, and unstaking requires a 20-day cooldown plus a 2-day withdrawal window. The BGD design proposal establishes that stkGHO is the main coverage asset for GHO bad debt inside a GHO-specific Safety Pool, that slashing is automated and precise, that each stk asset defines its exchange rate as a function of slashing, and that multiple staked assets covering GHO would be slashed proportionally. The GHO facilitator documentation establishes that underlying GHO is minted by governance-approved facilitators (Aave V3, CCIP, GSM, flashmint) under governance-set bucket capacities rather than by an stkGHO-local vault system. On-chain at the pinned block: asset() on 0x4f827a63755855cdf3e8f3bcd20265c833f15033 returned GHO 0x40D16FC0246aD3160Ccc09B8D0D3A2cD28aE6C2f; totalSupply() returned 14,553,497.911194915956083757 stkGHO; convertToAssets(totalSupply) returned exactly the same integer, an underlying conversion ratio of 1.0. Blockscout's verified-contract read names the proxy a TransparentUpgradeableProxy with implementation 0x75e8aC0c063B6966E2A9954adEdf39BdE9370197 (UmbrellaStakeToken), consistent with the staking-receipt design. collateralizationParameters and liquidationMechanics are structurally not applicable: the wrapper originates no borrower debt and runs no collateral liquidation pool, so both CDP ratios are null with cited not-applicable rationales rather than measured numbers. Backstop is limited: the holder's own stake is the first-loss capital for GHO deficits, and the only deeper layer evidenced is the governance-configured deficit offset, which is a sized first-tranche buffer rather than an unconditional recapitalization commitment. Branch isolation is limited: Umbrella documents slashing isolation to the GHO-Ethereum pair, but the GHO deficits it absorbs arise from a shared multi-facilitator issuance system whose bucket caps provide only bounded isolation. Shutdown and bad-debt handling is limited: the documented path is automated slashing and burn of this very token plus emergency mechanisms, with no evidenced facility that recapitalizes stkGHO holders after a deficit. Structural redemption is limited: convertToAssets(totalSupply) is 1:1 and permissionless in design, but redemption is time-gated by the documented 20-day cooldown and 2-day window and remains slash-impaired during that period; this makes no claim about GHO's own exit quality. NOT established: the current deficit-offset size for the GHO pair, any max slashable percentage bound (getter calls reverted at the pinned block), the share of GHO facilitator debt actually covered by the stkGHO stake, and any commitment beyond the documented offset that would absorb deficits ahead of stakers.

collateralizationRatio.rationale: stkGHO is a staking receipt over GHO and originates no borrower collateral positions; the underlying GHO is minted by facilitators against heterogeneous shared lending markets, so no stkGHO collateralization ratio exists.

liquidationCapacityRatio.rationale: stkGHO operates no collateral-liquidation pool; its slashing is deficit coverage of the underlying GHO system, not liquidation of borrower collateral.

collateralizationParameters.rationale: stkGHO is an ERC-4626-style staking receipt over GHO and has no local MCR/LTV or collateral-pricing parameters.

liquidationMechanics.rationale: The wrapper creates no borrower positions and liquidates no collateral; automated slashing for deficit coverage is not a collateral liquidation mechanism.

overlays.notes: steakUSDC is an immutable Morpho Vault V2 ERC-4626 vault over USDC curated by Steakhouse Financial. CLAIM AND SEGREGATION (limited): The binding Steakhouse DeFi Vaults Terms of Use establish that Carniceria Tropical Inc. (Panama) acts solely as vault curator over Morpho's self-executing contracts, that it does not possess or control user cryptoassets, that the applicable smart contracts govern distribution of funds, and that users interact from self-custodial wallets — positively establishing a non-custodial structure where the holder claim is the code-enforced ERC-4626 redemption. The Morpho Vault V2 README documents that all contracts are immutable and that users can exit at any time, including in-kind redemption via the permissionless forceDeallocate function even when underlying markets are illiquid (penalty up to 2%). The terms simultaneously disclaim any custodian, agent, or fiduciary relationship and cap liability at USD 1,000, and create NO legal claim, trust, or segregated reserve — so the claim rests on self-reported protocol documentation and immutable code only, which caps this at limited rather than adequate. CUSTODY CONTINUITY (limited): Reserves are USDC held by immutable Vault V2 contracts and their adapters in Morpho markets; there is no named off-chain custodian and no rehypothecation path. Steakhouse's controls documentation describes a five-of-quorum owner Safe, 7-day timelocks on new market onboarding, and an Aragon DAO guardian veto; the Supervisor v2 documentation describes a permanent Sentinel role and guardian veto over material owner actions, and its documented Ethereum Supervisor address 0x4D7bd498Bb24098Ca281C05519629c605407f71d exactly matches owner() read on-chain at block 25572050 (asset()=USDC, EIP-1967 implementation slot=0, curator()=0x827e86072B06674a077f592A531dcE4590aDeCdB). Curator failure therefore does not orphan assets, but allocation discretion remains with curator/owner roles and there is no custodian-diversification or independent custody framework. ASSURANCE AND RECONCILIATION (limited): ERC-4626 accounting is continuously reconcilable on-chain — at block 25572050, totalAssets()=75,851,755.50 USDC against totalSupply()=73,962,369.69 shares (share price ~1.0255 USDC) — and the Vault V2 codebase carries an extensive published audit suite (Spearbit 2025-05/2025-08/2025-09, Zellic 2025-07, Blackthorn 2025-09 and 2025-12, ChainSecurity 2025-09, Certora adapter review 2025-12, plus a 2025-07 competition) while the Supervisor v2 contract has a February 2026 Cantina audit. What was NOT established: no independent financial attestation or examination reconciling reserves to circulation exists; Steakhouse publishes no reserve attestations, and the terms disclaim responsibility for information accuracy. All tiers limited: the structure is well documented in binding terms plus protocol docs and verified on-chain, but there is no legal segregation and no independent assurance.

Measured at finalized Ethereum block 25572002 via eth_call on eth.drpc.org, cross-checked with identical values on ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com. The docs registry (contracts page) enumerates 12 markets; the MarketCreator event set confirmed by prior Pharos control reviews adds the msETH/WETH market, giving the complete set of 13 isMinter markets. For each market I read totalCollateral(), collatDecimals(), collatOracle().latestAnswer(true), MarketViewer.totalDebt(market) (which the verified MarketViewer source defines as badDebt + totalDebtShares x current debt index), maxLTV(), liquidationThreshold() and badDebt(). Per-market maxLTV is 72-90% and liquidation thresholds 76-91.5%; every market reports badDebt() = 0. Collateral value sums to 4,514,306.16 USD at each market's own oracle price; total market debt is 3,438,780.85 USG, giving collateralizationRatio 1.312764 = collateral value over total market debt. Denominator note: USG totalSupply is 43,438,453.33, but the holder list shows exactly 20,000,000 USG sitting idle in each of the two peg keeper contracts (mintPegKeeper pre-minted inventory, PegKeeperV2 debt() = 0, i.e. none of it has been deployed into the pools); supply minus this inventory is 3,438,453.33, reconciling with market debt within 327.52 USG (0.01%), so market debt is the economically outstanding USG. The conservative total-supply denominator gives 0.103924 and is recorded in analogousMetrics. The msETH/WETH market moved from staged (zero debt cap, zero debt at block 25531905) to live with 463,482.69 USG debt, so all 13 markets now carry debt. The two peg pools hold 475,846.98 USDC and 550,087.44 frxUSD of counterparty assets (recorded in analogousMetrics, not counted as borrower collateral). Liquidation mechanics per the health docs: anyone may repay an underwater loan's USG debt and take the collateral at a profit (20% fee on positive liquidation profit minted to the fee treasury, per the verified market source), collateral can be sold through the zapping proxy, and Tangent runs its own liquidation bot so liquidations proceed even when externally unprofitable; no Stability Pool or other committed capital pool exists anywhere in the reviewed contracts, so backstop is weak. Bad debt per the health docs: the DAO seizes underwater collateral to the fee treasury, bad debt is registered market-locally, anyone can burn USG via repayBadDebt, and the affected market's interest and earnings are redirected to recovery until repaid; there is no unconditional recapitalization commitment and no documented global shutdown, so shutdownAndBadDebt is limited. Branch isolation is adequate: 13 isolated markets with per-market debt caps (maxMarketDebt), market-local bad debt and market-local earnings recovery, all read on-chain. Structural redemption is weak: the overview and peg-stability docs state explicitly that USG does not use redemptions and cannot be redeemed for its collateral; the peg rests on Peg Keepers (crvUSD-fork, permissionless deposit/withdraw against USG/USDC and USG/frxUSD pools) plus price-dependent interest and rewards deduction. NOT established: position-level collateral weights per market (only aggregate protocol-priced values), any committed liquidation or insurance capital (none found), any redemption or hard peg-floor path (docs explicitly disclaim it), and DAO multisig control parameters (out of scope for this component set; the owner Safe's pause and parameter powers were only verified in the separate Pharos control review, not re-derived here).

liquidationCapacityRatio.rationale: Tangent liquidations are funded by external liquidators who repay an underwater position's USG debt in exchange for its collateral at a profit, optionally sold through the zapping proxy; the protocol documentation describes no Stability Pool or any USG-dedicated capital pool contractually committed to debt offset, and the Tangent-operated liquidation bot is an operational fallback rather than committed capital. The fee treasury receives liquidation fees and interest but is not contractually committed to debt offset; residual bad debt is handled by DAO seizure and permissionless repayBadDebt burns, evidenced under shutdownAndBadDebt.

Measured at Citrea mainnet block 10237871 (2026-07-20T20:07:43Z, chain id 4114) via eth_call against the documented contract addresses. JUSD is a Frankencoin/d-EURO architecture fork, but the measurement shows its collateralized-minting engine is currently inert and the token is in practice a 1:1 wrapper over one bridged stablecoin. totalSupply() = 56650.338747215709827641 JUSD. The three StablecoinBridge contracts report minted() of 56650.262522057361950443 (USDT.e), 0.067761203702540029 (USDC.e) and 0.008463954645337169 (ctUSD), which sum to exactly totalSupply to the last wei; minterReserve() is 0. Bridge-route minting therefore accounts for 100.000000% of supply and position-minted JUSD is exactly zero, so no collateralized position is outstanding for the documented CDP machinery to govern. The bridges hold 56650.342015 units of underlying (USDT.e 56650.262935, USDC.e 0.069368, ctUSD 0.009712), giving collateralizationRatio 1.000000058 - fully backed but with no overcollateralization whatsoever, and 99.99986% of that backing is a single asset, bridged Tether USDT.e. Collateralization parameters: the position documentation defines owner-set liquidation prices, per-position minimum collateral and challenge periods, but these govern 0% of supply; the live route is the bridge, whose on-chain limit() reads 1e20 raw against a 6-decimal underlying (about 1e14 tokens), i.e. effectively uncapped 1:1 minting against USDT.e, and whose horizon() is 2030-01-21T04:33:31Z. NOT established: any protocol-enforced minimum collateral ratio, any debt ceiling that is economically binding, and whether any position has ever been opened. Liquidation mechanics are documented (permissionless challenges, Dutch auctions, 2% challenger reward, oracle-free bid-switching inherited from the audited Frankencoin design) but are inert at zero position debt, and the bridge route has no liquidation path at all - rated limited rather than adequate because the mechanism currently protects nothing. Backstop: equity() = 172.402256388877894161 JUSD against 56650.34 supply = 0.3043% equity coverage, with minterReserve() at 0, so the loss-absorbing layer is 0.30% of supply against a backing book that is essentially 100% USDT.e counterparty and bridge-contract risk. NOT established: any pre-funded backstop beyond JUICE equity, and JUICE's quoted price() of 0.000542401159122236 against a 3178500.88 share supply was not independently corroborated as realisable value. Branch isolation: each bridge is a separate contract with its own limit and horizon and each position would be a separate single-collateral contract, but with 99.99986% of backing in one bridged asset the documented isolation delivers no practical diversification - limited. Shutdown and bad debt: no global settlement or shutdown mechanism exists; bad debt would be socialised by minting uncovered JUSD as in the parent Frankencoin design - limited. NOT established: the post-horizon behaviour of the bridges after 2030-01-21 was read from contract state but the redemption consequences were not confirmed against a pinned source commit. Structural redemption is the one component measured as adequate: the StablecoinBridge burn path is permissionless and the bridges verifiably hold 100.000006% of the underlying needed to honour every outstanding JUSD at 1:1 at the measured block, so every holder has a funded, contract-enforced exit that does not depend on an auction or a governance decision. NOT established: whether that exit survives a USDT.e depeg, freeze or blacklist event, since the redemption asset is itself a blacklistable third-party stablecoin, and no bridge-level circuit breaker was found. NOT established more broadly: the CDP archetype's parameters could not be exercised against live positions because none exist, so this review measures a wrapper, not a working CDP; if positions are opened later the collateralizationParameters, liquidationMechanics and branchIsolation ratings should be re-derived rather than carried forward.

overlays.notes: DUSD is the Dialectic-curated Makina Machine share over USDC, not a par-redeemable issuer dollar. The Makina strategy API names Dialectic as the DUSD operator, and latest Ethereum PublicNode reads at block 25647044 returned operator() = mechanic() = 0x425BbC2cfF0c7E7960baA9BaC2f0Cb67B41d3beF for Machine 0x6b006870c83b1cd49e766ac9209f8d68763df721. The official team-supplied Dialectic Meccanico Machine Terms v1.2 (SHA-256 beb0e92828a923048b19f78837b3482f7c3f4075052df81e8a34f2bbbcc7637c; expected publication URL pending during the 2026-07-30 review) identify Dialectic Meccanico Ltd as Operator and apply to Machines identified by on-chain operator attribution and/or an Operator Agreement. The holder's on-chain claim remains a code-mediated share claim against Machine AUM: deposits mint shares through DirectDepositor at the current share price, redemptions enter the AsyncRedeemer FIFO queue with a 12-hour minimum finalization delay and operator-liquidity dependency, and the share price is AUM divided by share supply in USDC terms. On-chain reads at Ethereum block 25636769 verified the share token 0x1e33e98af620f1d563fcd3cfd3c75ace841204ef, Machine 0x6b006870c83b1cd49e766ac9209f8d68763df721, accountingToken() = Circle USDC, shareToken() = the DUSD share token, shareLimit() = 75,000,000e18, totalSupply() = 5,618,599.537452822458574240 shares, and recoveryMode() = false. CLAIM AND SEGREGATION is weak from affirmative legal evidence: the Machine Terms establish that acquisitions are sales by the Operator as principal, settlement assets and Machine assets become or remain the Operator's property, Users have no legal/equitable/proprietary/custody/trust/underlying/yield/governance/priority/bankruptcy-remote rights, buybacks are discretionary rather than contractual redemption rights, and Machine cessation or Operator insolvency creates no holder asset-return process or Makina Party claim. The code-mediated share accounting and technical Machine/Caliber controls remain relevant implementation facts, but they do not cure the legal claim and segregation deficiency. CUSTODY CONTINUITY is limited: Makina documentation and the reviewed allocation API identify strategy deployment through approved Calibers into protocol positions, and the Machine/fee/governance graph was verified on-chain, but assets are actively deployed into Morpho, Aave, Pareto/FalconX, Re, and Royco exposures and no independent custodian-continuity, trustee-custody, legal segregation, or bankruptcy-remote operator-replacement framework was established. overlays.notes: JPYSC is a trust-type Type III electronic payment instrument, so fiat-cash is the correct runtime archetype. The dated governing terms give each holder a direct redemption claim against SBI Shinsei Trust, specify that trust property is separate from the trustee's own estate and ordinarily bankruptcy-remote, and set a standard redemption period of two business days after acceptance. The trustee is named and the trust assets are legally constrained to yen deposits and Japanese government bonds, but underlying deposit banks, provider allocations, successor-trustee procedures, and rehypothecation controls are not fully disclosed; claim and custody therefore remain limited rather than adequate/strong. The statutory page reports at 2026-06-30 19:00 exactly JPY 10,008,294,794 issued against JPY 10,008,304,794 in the trust deposit account. That is a dated issuer/trustee assets-to-liabilities reconciliation under a statutory disclosure regime, but the governing terms explicitly state that issuance operations are not audited and no later independent attestation or current cash/JGB split is published, so assurance is limited.
